verdict: 2026-07-29 11:08:16 PDT — The core shape is appropriately small and uses existing React/Zoom primitives; no dependency already provides this Zoom-specific recovery lifecycle. It is not yet sound, however, because send-outcome state and rendering-context ownership are not fully centralized.

findings.title: Hide does not fully supersede an in-flight reopen
findings.claim: `rebuildOverlay` checks intent after awaiting `start`, but if Hide calls `closeRenderingContext` while that start is pending, the operations remain concurrent and unordered. When start later completes, recovery skips posting but never closes the possibly recreated context. The UI can therefore say “Show cost on video” while a rendering context remains active, violating AC3 and the approved Hide invariant.
findings.alternative: Give rendering-context mutations one serialized, generation-aware owner. Hide should advance the generation and set desired state off; after any awaited start, a stale generation must perform a compensating close. A small controller or promise queue used by both Hide and automatic recovery would enforce last-intent-wins.
findings.win: Eliminates concurrent start/close ownership and one hidden-UI/live-context state, making “Hide always wins” an enforced invariant rather than a timing assumption.

findings.title: Most successful sends bypass the recovery state machine
findings.claim: Only the interval send at line 181 feeds its result to `runPostRecovery`. Sends performed during start, the fresh-snapshot effect, and `rebuildOverlay` ignore their outcomes. Consequently, a successful post after failures does not necessarily reset `consecutiveFailures` as AC1 requires; the state also survives Hide→Show, so one failure in a new overlay run can complete an old run's threshold and trigger an early rebuild.
findings.alternative: Create one observed send boundary that owns `adapter.postMessage` plus the outcome transition, and route every send through it. Treat Hide/new overlay generations as explicit reset transitions; the recovery controller can consume the reducer's rebuild effect without recursively rebuilding from its own validation post.
findings.win: Removes three fire-and-forget outcome paths, prevents stale failure state crossing overlay lifecycles, and centralizes the AC1 reset invariant in one place.
